label: Thursday evening, trudging back towards King's Pyland
quote: remarked Holmes as we trudged along together
note: Holmes speaks of Silas Brown and the horse, and says they go back to London by the night train (¶144–156). Watson can draw nothing more from him until they reach the trainer's house (¶157).

label: That morning, when Silas Brown, first down, saw a strange horse wandering over the moor
quote: when according to his custom he was the first down, he perceived a strange horse wandering over the moor
note: This is Holmes's account of what he described to Brown. He calls it 'that morning', and a reader takes it to be the morning after the night of the crime. Brown goes out to the horse and recognises the white forehead.

label: That morning, when Silas Brown first set out to lead the horse back to King's Pyland
quote: his first impulse had been to lead him back to King’s Pyland
note: This is Holmes's account. It matches the double track turning off towards King's Pyland (¶122).

label: That morning, when Silas Brown led the horse back and hid it at Mapleton
quote: how he had led it back and concealed it at Mapleton
note: This is Holmes's account. It matches the return track to the Mapleton gates (¶122–124). Brown means to hide the horse until the race is over (t.race). Watson's 'But his stables had been searched?' (¶147) implies the horse was there when the stables were searched (t.gregory_mapleton). The text does not order the two points strictly.

label: Thursday evening, back at the trainer's house, in the parlour
quote: until we were back at the trainer’s house. The Colonel and the Inspector were awaiting us in the parlour
note: Holmes announces the night-express, asks for the photograph and goes out to question the maid. The Colonel speaks to Watson while Holmes is away, and then Holmes comes back (¶158–168).

label: Thursday evening, Holmes out of the room to question the maid
quote: I have a question which I should like to put to the maid

label: Thursday evening, stepping into the carriage, Holmes asks the stable-lad about the sheep
quote: As we stepped into the carriage one of the stable-lads held the door open for us
note: The talk with Gregory about the dog in the night-time follows as they drive off (¶175–182).

label: Of late, when three of the sheep in the paddock went lame
quote: three of them have gone lame, sir
note: The lad says it was 'of late' (¶172). The text gives no other date.

label: In the night-time, when the dog did nothing
quote: The dog did nothing in the night-time
note: A reader takes this to be the night of the crime, but the text does not say which hour.

label: Thursday night, the night train back to London
quote: we both go back to London by the night train
note: This is planned. ¶158 calls it 'the night-express'.
This was planned at ¶112. It begins at ¶175 with 'Drive on, coachman!', after the talk with the stable-lad.
